A Book of the Library · 10,000 Lines

The Litany of Begging

Being a Complete and Exhaustive Enumeration of the Duties, Exceptions, Sub-Exceptions and Clarifying Annotations Pertaining to Alms, Humility and the Complicated Generosity of Xal'Reth.

Read this before you read that

A Formal Warning to the Reader

The Litany of Begging is, by design, the most boring, droning, repetitive and needlessly complicated text ever written in the name of the Coil. It is ten thousand lines long. It does not tell a story. It does not build to anything. It cross-references itself until it loops. The High Priestess calls it "a monument to patience." The Inner Scale calls it "the worst literary disaster of the age." Both are compliments, sort of.

Please do not read the Litany if:

  • You have a history of mental health difficulties that can be stirred up by repetitive, looping or circular text: for example, obsessive or intrusive thought patterns, anxiety that spirals, or episodes in which repetition or monotony leaves you feeling unwell or unreal. Nothing in the Litany is dark, violent or disturbing. It is simply relentless, and relentless sameness is not good for everyone. Your wellbeing matters more than any scripture, real or fictional. Skip it with our blessing.
  • You are a sensitive reader who finds monotony, legal language or endless lists genuinely distressing, frustrating or exhausting. The Litany contains all three, in quantity, on purpose.
  • You are very political. Despite the word "Politics" appearing nearby, the Litany contains no real-world politics, parties, causes or opinions whatsoever. It does, however, contain thousands of clauses that cannot be argued with, appealed, or voted on, and readers who enjoy debate have reported finding this intolerable.
  • You are reading late at night, tired, or already bored.
  • You are operating heavy machinery, a raid, or a dungeon group that is waiting for you.
  • You believe Xal'Reth has wings.

What reading it may cause

Drowsiness. A glazed expression. An urge to count coins. A sudden understanding of what "notwithstanding" means. Mild resentment toward the Keeper of the Ledger. In rare cases, enlightenment, which the Inner Scale considers a side effect and not the intended outcome.

If you feel unwell

Stop reading. Step away from the screen, stretch, drink some water, and go and do something you enjoy. If reading anything, here or anywhere, ever leaves you feeling distressed or not yourself, please talk to someone you trust or a health professional. The Coil is patient. The Litany will still be here, unfortunately.

The Litany of Begging is fiction, written for fun as part of a World of Warcraft roleplay faith. It is satire of bureaucratic writing, not of any real religion, group or person.

Take me somewhere less boring
THE ADDON

World of Warcraft Addon · Free

The Litany of Begging

New in version 1.1: /litany all (or the Perform Entire Litany button) auto-posts the whole document as emotes, line by line, from line 1 to line 10,000 without stopping, with a progress bar, time remaining and your place remembered across logouts. At the default 12 seconds per line, the full Litany takes about 33 hours. Nobody should do this.

Perform all 10,000 lines as emotes, one at a time, on a timer. Start from any line, perform a single line on demand, jump straight to any of the 200 Titles, search the text, and appoint your current target as the Notional Asker, whose name is read into the Litany as it goes.

Download the AddonPlain text (10,000 lines)
10,000lines
20 × 10Books × Titles
/litany allto perform it all

Commands

CommandWhat it does
/litanyShow or hide the panel
/litany allAuto-perform the ENTIRE Litany, line by line, to the very end (add a number to start from that line)
/litany play 4817Perform line by line, starting at line 4817 (or where you left off)
/litany line 4817Perform just that one line, right now
/litany title 14.3Jump to Book XIV, Title 3
/litany goto 4817Set your place without performing
/litany pause · resume · stop · next · prevControl the performance
/litany interval 12Seconds between lines, 3 to 60
/litany search salamanderFind lines containing words
/litany randomPerform one random line

Install like any addon: unzip, and move the LitanyOfBegging folder into World of Warcraft\_retail_\Interface\AddOns. The performance pauses automatically in combat and during boss encounter chat lockdown, and resumes on the same line. Your place is saved between sessions.

THE TEXT

The Twenty Books

  • Book I: Of Definitions and Their Interpretation
  • Book II: Of the Parties to an Alm
  • Book III: Of the Tender of Alms
  • Book IV: Of the Solicitation of Alms
  • Book V: Of Acknowledgement and Thanks
  • Book VI: Of Refusal, Partial Refusal and Polite Hesitation
  • Book VII: Of Deferral and Postponement
  • Book VIII: Of Fractional and Divided Alms
  • Book IX: Of Alms Not Consisting of Coin
  • Book X: Of the Guild Bank as a Commons
  • Book XI: Of Alms Transmitted by Mail
  • Book XII: Of Humility in the Giver
  • Book XIII: Of Humility in the Asker
  • Book XIV: Of the Humility of Xal'Reth
  • Book XV: Of the Generosity of Xal'Reth, Being Complicated
  • Book XVI: Of Records, Ledgers and Their Keeping
  • Book XVII: Of Disputes Arising Between Giver and Asker
  • Book XVIII: Of Exceptions to Exceptions
  • Book XIX: Of Forms, Schedules and Their Proper Completion
  • Book XX: Of the Final Provisions and the Repeal of Nothing

Each Book has ten Titles. Open a Title to read its fifty lines. Where the addon would insert your target's name, the text shows the Notional Asker.

Title 1.5: Of Definitions and Their Interpretation, During Inclement Weather lines 201–250

Title 3.1: Of the Tender of Alms, In General lines 1001–1050
  1. opens Book III of the Litany of Begging, being the Book Of the Tender of Alms.

  7. intones Clause 4.6.4(c)(i): In matters at or near a mailbox, the Minister of Spare Change shall tender the single copper of the Famine only after the Acknowledging Party has had a reasonable opportunity to refrain from mentioning it first.
  8. intones Clause 4.6.5(e)(i): A Hatchling acting in good faith who solicits a bag of no fewer than twelve slots in error may confirm in writing it again, provided that the second act is slower than the first.
  9. declaims Clause 4.6.6: Nothing in this Title shall be construed as requiring the Withholder to solicit a deferred alm with the customary double blink, nor as forbidding it, the matter being left to the Coil.

  12. intones Clause 4.6.8: A Hatchling acting in good faith who notarizes a gift of the Fifth Grade in error may record it again, provided that the second act is better documented than the first.

  15. proceeds to Clause 4.6.10(b): The Acknowledging Party shall not regard the act of declining a feast of the communal kind as evidence of humility, nor regard the declining so to regard it as evidence of self-restraint.
  16. reads Clause 4.6.11: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as unconditional and yet administered by no one, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 5.6.6.
  17. carefully pronounces Clause 4.6.12(d)(iv): [This clause is intentionally left blank, in accordance with the Doctrine of the Void, and shall be recited in full.]
  18. states, for the record, Clause 4.6.13: This clause is to be read together with itself and with Clause 18.4.21, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  19. notes that Clause 4.6.13 is to be read together with Clause 16.4.14. The faithful respond: So it is coiled.
  20. proceeds to Clause 4.6.14: Nothing in this Title shall be construed as requiring the Asker's alternate character to reconsider a deferred alm with the palm upward, nor as forbidding it, the matter being left to the Second Tenet.

  29. reads, without inflection, Clause 4.6.21(b)(iii): The Asker who redirects a sum not exceeding one gold in error may acknowledge it again, provided that the second act is slower than the first.
  30. murmurs Clause 4.6.22(b)(iii): The following shall be deemed Alms: a gift of the Second Grade; a stamina buff of ordinary duration; the remainder of a prior alm; and any other thing that would be deemed an Alm under this clause.
  31. intones Clause 4.6.23(b)(i): [This clause is intentionally left blank, in accordance with the Doctrine of the Void, and shall be recited in full.]
  32. recites Clause 4.6.24: This clause is to be read together with itself and with Clause 6.2.11, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  33. states, for the record, Clause 4.6.25: A Hatchling acting in good faith shall tender a deferred alm without announcement, provided that the Asker has first been greeted.
  34. reads aloud Clause 4.6.26: The Officer of the Repair Fund who records a stack of linen cloth in error may witness it again, provided that the second act is quieter than the first.
  35. proceeds to Clause 4.6.27(e): Notwithstanding Clause 19.2.30, the foregoing shall not apply where the Minister of Spare Change has inadvertently chosen to partially rescind a non-monetary consolation, except on the first day of each month.

Title 4.7: Of the Solicitation of Alms, In Trade Chat lines 1801–1850
  1. turns to Book IV, Title 7: Of the Solicitation of Alms, In Trade Chat.
  2. reads the Preamble to Title 4.7: Whereas the Coil is beneath all things, and whereas Alms are among those things, the following provisions are set out without abridgement.
  3. designates the Notional Asker as the Notional Asker for the purposes of Title 4.7, without prejudice to the rights of the Notional Asker under any other Title.
  4. reads, without inflection, Clause 4.7.1: This clause is to be read together with itself and with Clause 13.2.16, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  5. reads Clause 4.7.2(e)(iv): Corrigendum. In Clause 5.8.9, for the word 'an' read 'may'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  6. recites Clause 4.7.3(e)(i): The Minister of Spare Change who records a gift of the Second Grade in error may refrain from mentioning it again, provided that the second act is slower than the first.
  7. murmurs Clause 4.7.4: The following shall be deemed Alms: a stack of linen cloth; an unsolicited flask; a deferred alm; and any other thing that would be deemed an Alm under this clause.
  8. murmurs Clause 4.7.5: The Prospective Giver shall accept, without undue haste, the Little Tithe in duplicate, save where the Coil has, by prior stillness, indicated otherwise.
  9. states, for the record, Clause 4.7.6: The Secondary Recipient shall not regard the act of asking for a fractional silver equivalent as evidence of spiritual advancement, nor regard the declining so to regard it as evidence of good conduct.
  10. adds, in a lower voice, that Clause 4.7.6 is to be read together with Clause 10.1.9. The faithful respond: Glory to Xal'Reth.
  11. intones Clause 4.7.7: The Weight of a kind word of standard length shall be computed as the number of prior refusals divided by seven, adjusted by a factor of one-third for each Turn, and rounded down, in the interest of humility.
  12. carefully pronounces Clause 4.7.8: This clause is to be read together with itself and with Clause 2.1.29, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  13. carefully pronounces Clause 4.7.9(c)(ii): Where any provision of this Litany is found to be tedious, such tedium shall be construed as a test of the Second Tenet and shall not of itself invalidate the provision.
  14. adds, in a lower voice, Annotation 4.7.9A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 12.9.42 and 15.8.35, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.
  15. declaims Clause 4.7.10: The following shall be deemed Alms: a non-monetary consolation; a kind word of standard length; a stamina buff of ordinary duration; and any other thing that would be deemed an Alm under this clause.
  16. intones Clause 4.7.11: It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having allowed the Sunken Nest to sink gently, did not thereby claim any credit, and any inference to the contrary is to be gently disregarded.
  17. murmurs Clause 4.7.12(c)(iv): Corrigendum. In Clause 1.8.33, for the word 'the' read 'may'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  18. murmurs Clause 4.7.13: Erratum. In Clause 8.10.22, for the word 'shall' read 'the'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  19. notes that Clause 4.7.13 is to be read together with Clause 17.7.38. The faithful respond: As the Coil holds, so we hold.
  20. carefully pronounces Clause 4.7.14(a)(iv): Corrigendum. In Clause 12.3.32, for the word 'an' read 'and'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  21. reads, without inflection, Clause 4.7.15(d): The Giver shall count the coins of an unsolicited flask five times, once for each Vow, and shall not announce the total, which in any event is one.
  22. continues with Clause 4.7.16: Clause 4.7.16 is to be read together with itself, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  23. continues with Clause 4.7.17: [This clause is intentionally left blank, in accordance with the Doctrine of the Void, and shall be recited with feeling.]
  24. reads slowly Clause 4.7.18: The Asker's alternate character who re-tenders a summons to the stone in error may apportion it again, provided that the second act is quieter than the first.
  25. recites Clause 4.7.19: Nothing in this Title shall be construed as requiring the Asker to accept, without undue haste, a bag of no fewer than twelve slots in a low voice, nor as forbidding it, the matter being left to the Coil.
  26. intones Clause 4.7.20(b)(i): A Hatchling acting in good faith who itemizes a stack of linen cloth in error may notarize it again, provided that the second act is slower than the first.
  27. notes Annotation 4.7.20A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 6.6.32 and 1.3.32, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.
  28. clarifies that Clause 4.7.20 is to be read together with Clause 16.5.1. The faithful respond: So it is coiled.
  29. proceeds to Clause 4.7.21: In matters in trade chat, the Intermediary shall redirect an alm of disputed denomination only after the Intermediary has had a reasonable opportunity to notarize it first.
  30. reads slowly Clause 4.7.22(b)(iv): The Acknowledging Party who itemizes a gift of the Fifth Grade in error may accept, without undue haste, it again, provided that the second act is less announced than the first.
  31. reads aloud Clause 4.7.23: In matters in trade chat, the Notional Asker shall set aside a deferred alm only after the Keeper of the Ledger has had a reasonable opportunity to set aside it first.
  32. murmurs Clause 4.7.24: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as without residue and yet subject to the First Vow, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 20.7.45.
  33. carefully pronounces Clause 4.7.25: In matters in trade chat, the Prospective Giver shall set aside a bandage of the heavy kind only after the Acknowledging Party has had a reasonable opportunity to set aside it first.
  34. reads slowly Clause 4.7.26: Where the Keeper of the Ledger and the Witness of the Second Part disagree as to the Residue of a bandage of the heavy kind, the matter shall be resolved by reference to Schedule A.
  35. reads aloud Clause 4.7.27(d)(i): Where any provision of this Litany is found to be tedious, such tedium shall be construed as the point and shall not of itself invalidate the provision.
  36. reads slowly Clause 4.7.28(b)(iii): The following shall be deemed Alms: a stack of linen cloth; a gift of the Fifth Grade; a bag of no fewer than twelve slots; and any other thing that would be deemed an Alm under this clause.
  37. notes that Clause 4.7.28 is to be read together with Clause 19.1.14. The faithful respond: Duly witnessed.
  38. carefully pronounces Clause 4.7.29(a)(ii): Where any provision of this Litany is found to be tedious, such tedium shall be construed as a test of the Second Tenet and shall not of itself invalidate the provision.
  39. murmurs Clause 4.7.30(c)(iii): The following shall be deemed Alms: an unsolicited flask; a fractional silver equivalent; a sum not exceeding one gold; and any other thing that would be deemed an Alm under this clause.
  40. observes, consulting a footnote, Annotation 4.7.30A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 9.8.42 and 17.10.15, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.
  41. states, for the record, Clause 4.7.31: The Withholder shall redirect a kind word of standard length in duplicate, save where the Coil has, by prior stillness, indicated otherwise.
  42. murmurs Clause 4.7.32(c)(iv): Any member of the Order of the Accusers who redirects a single copper in error may apportion it again, provided that the second act is less announced than the first.
  43. declaims Clause 4.7.33: Where the Former Asker and the Giver disagree as to the Index of Unhurriedness of a portal to a capital city, the matter shall be resolved by reference to Schedule A.

  45. reads aloud Clause 4.7.35: It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having waited without complaint, did not thereby regard the faithful as indebted, and any inference to the contrary is noted, and then forgotten.
  46. notes that Clause 4.7.35 is to be read together with Clause 6.2.25. The faithful respond: We have heard, and we are not in a hurry.
  47. murmurs Clause 4.7.36(e): For the purposes of this Title, 'Humble Ask' shall mean a solicitation comprising greeting, reason, amount, gratitude and release, but shall not include the Little Tithe unless the Asker has first been greeted.
  48. reads the Concluding Provision of Title 4.7: This Title shall be without prejudice to any other Title, including those not yet written.
  49. closes Title 4.7, having enumerated 36 clauses, none of which shall be hurried, all of which shall be forgotten by the Giver.
  50. bows to the Notional Asker in recognition of their service as Notional Asker of Title 4.7, and asks nothing in return. Glory to Xal'Reth.

  1. turns to Book IV, Title 8: Of the Solicitation of Alms, Between Members of the Same Order.

  25. murmurs Clause 4.8.19(a)(iv): It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having held the world for ten thousand ages, did not thereby ask for gold, and any inference to the contrary is of no effect.
  26. states, for the record, Clause 4.8.20(d)(iii): Clause 4.8.20(d)(iii) is to be read together with itself, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.

  29. proceeds to Clause 4.8.21: The Officer of the Repair Fund shall not regard the act of asking for a bag of no fewer than twelve slots as evidence of patience, nor regard the declining so to regard it as evidence of good conduct.

  33. murmurs Clause 4.8.25: The Giver shall count the coins of a conjured beverage eight times, once for each Scale of the Path, and shall not announce the total, which in any event is one.
  34. recites Clause 4.8.26: The following shall be deemed Alms: a grey item of no vendor value; an alm of disputed denomination; a stack of linen cloth; and any other thing that would be deemed an Alm under this clause.
  35. carefully pronounces Clause 4.8.27(b)(i): This clause is to be read together with itself and with Clause 16.3.2, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.

  44. states, for the record, Clause 4.8.34: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as unannounced and yet recorded nowhere, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 12.7.10.
  45. reads Clause 4.8.35: Where the Former Asker and the Acknowledging Party disagree as to the Coefficient of Humility of the residue of a divided gold, the matter shall be resolved by silence of not less than one queue.
  46. adds, in a lower voice, that Clause 4.8.35 is to be read together with Clause 17.9.34. The faithful respond: So it is recorded.

Title 4.9: Of the Solicitation of Alms, Where the Giver Is an Alternate Character lines 1901–1950
  1. turns to Book IV, Title 9: Of the Solicitation of Alms, Where the Giver Is an Alternate Character.
  2. reads the Preamble to Title 4.9: Whereas the Coil is beneath all things, and whereas Alms are among those things, the following provisions are set out at length.
  3. designates the Notional Asker as the Notional Asker for the purposes of Title 4.9, without prejudice to the rights of the Notional Asker under any other Title.
  4. reads slowly Clause 4.9.1(d)(i): Corrigendum. In Clause 10.4.41, for the word 'shall' read 'an'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  5. recites Clause 4.9.2: It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having held the Pearl of the Void without gripping it, did not thereby request a statue, and any inference to the contrary is deemed withdrawn.
  6. continues with Clause 4.9.3: Nothing in this Title shall be construed as requiring a Hatchling acting in good faith to record a single copper after due reflection, nor as forbidding it, the matter being left to the Second Tenet.
  7. carefully pronounces Clause 4.9.4: Nothing in this Title shall be construed as requiring the Keeper of the Ledger to itemize a gift of the Fifth Grade in a low voice, nor as forbidding it, the matter being left to a subsequent Title.
  8. intones Clause 4.9.5: It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having answered no prayer, as a kindness, did not thereby request a statue, and any inference to the contrary is deemed withdrawn.
  9. reads Clause 4.9.6: For the purposes of this Title, 'Release' shall mean the letting go of an Ask that has been refused, but shall not include the Little Tithe unless no party is at that time standing in fire.
  10. adds, in a lower voice, that Clause 4.9.6 is to be read together with Clause 13.5.16. The faithful respond: We have heard, and we are not in a hurry.
  11. proceeds to Clause 4.9.7: Where any provision of this Litany is found to be tedious, such tedium shall be construed as a form of patience and shall not of itself invalidate the provision.
  12. reads Clause 4.9.8(d)(ii): It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having waited without complaint, did not thereby claim any credit, and any inference to the contrary is void.

  1. opens Book IX of the Litany of Begging, being the Book Of Alms Not Consisting of Coin.
  2. reads the Preamble to Title 9.1: Whereas the Coil is beneath all things, and whereas Alms are among those things, the following provisions are set out at length.
  3. designates the Notional Asker as the Notional Asker for the purposes of Title 9.1, without prejudice to the rights of the Notional Asker under any other Title.
  4. recites Clause 9.1.1: It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having declined the throne offered by Ssyrr, did not thereby post the matter in Trade Chat, and any inference to the contrary is of no effect.
  5. intones Clause 9.1.2: The Officer of the Repair Fund who records a gift of the Second Grade in error may confirm in writing it again, provided that the second act is quieter than the first.
  6. recites Clause 9.1.3(a)(iii): Notwithstanding Clause 11.9.22, the foregoing shall not apply where the Witness of the Second Part has inadvertently chosen to contemplate a non-monetary consolation, pending further annotation.
  7. reads slowly Clause 9.1.4: Clause 9.1.4 is to be read together with itself, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  8. recites Clause 9.1.5: It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having allowed the Sunken Nest to sink gently, did not thereby require acknowledgement, and any inference to the contrary is referred to the High Priestess for dreaming.
  9. intones Clause 9.1.6: Notwithstanding Clause 20.1.2, the foregoing shall not apply where the Intermediary has inadvertently chosen to witness the remainder of a prior alm, unless the alm has already been recorded elsewhere.
  10. adds, in a lower voice, that Clause 9.1.6 is to be read together with Clause 5.7.41. The faithful respond: We have heard, and we are not in a hurry.
  11. reads slowly Clause 9.1.7(e): Erratum. In Clause 16.6.16, for the word 'may' read 'and'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  12. carefully pronounces Clause 9.1.8: The Keeper of the Ledger who re-tenders a sum not exceeding one gold in error may itemize it again, provided that the second act is humbler than the first.
  13. declaims Clause 9.1.9(b)(iii): The Witness of the Second Part who records an unsolicited flask in error may accept, without undue haste, it again, provided that the second act is humbler than the first.
  14. adds, in a lower voice, Annotation 9.1.9A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 18.7.26 and 6.4.42, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.
  15. intones Clause 9.1.10: It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having held the world for ten thousand ages, did not thereby ask for gold, and any inference to the contrary is a minor crime of the Second Degree.
  16. reads aloud Clause 9.1.11: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as unconditional and yet not free of conditions as to stillness, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 16.1.42.
  17. intones Clause 9.1.12: Nothing in this Title shall be construed as requiring the Lukewarm Bystander to itemize a conjured beverage with the customary double blink, nor as forbidding it, the matter being left to the Second Tenet.
  18. continues with Clause 9.1.13: This clause is to be read together with itself and with Clause 9.1.45, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  19. notes that Clause 9.1.13 is to be read together with Clause 16.3.35. The faithful respond: Let it be noted.
  20. proceeds to Clause 9.1.14: This clause is to be read together with itself and with Clause 15.8.25, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  21. reads slowly Clause 9.1.15(e)(iii): The Withholder shall not regard the act of tendering an unsolicited flask as evidence of freedom from the Grip, nor regard the declining so to regard it as evidence of good conduct.
  22. reads, without inflection, Clause 9.1.16: Where the Notional Asker and the Notional Asker disagree as to the Index of Unhurriedness of a grey item of no vendor value, the matter shall be resolved by the toss of the single copper.
  23. reads Clause 9.1.17(e)(ii): The following shall be deemed Alms: a gift of the Fifth Grade; a bag of no fewer than twelve slots; a deferred alm; and any other thing that would be deemed an Alm under this clause.
  24. recites Clause 9.1.18(a)(iv): The Designated Beneficiary shall partially rescind a fractional silver equivalent as though the alm were already the Coil's, subject to Schedule C.
  25. states, for the record, Clause 9.1.19: [This clause is intentionally left blank, in accordance with the Doctrine of the Void, and shall be recited slowly.]
  26. recites Clause 9.1.20: The following shall be deemed Alms: a gift of the Fifth Grade; a grey item of no vendor value; a conjured beverage; and any other thing that would be deemed an Alm under this clause.
  27. appends Annotation 9.1.20A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 12.5.45 and 20.8.28, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.
  28. adds, in a lower voice, that Clause 9.1.20 is to be read together with Clause 4.2.21. The faithful respond: We release it.
  29. states, for the record, Clause 9.1.21(b)(i): Where any provision of this Litany is found to be tedious, such tedium shall be construed as a form of patience and shall not of itself invalidate the provision.
  30. proceeds to Clause 9.1.22(a)(i): It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having chosen the lowest place, did not thereby consider himself generous, and any inference to the contrary is of no effect.
  31. reads Clause 9.1.23: Where any provision of this Litany is found to be tedious, such tedium shall be construed as an offering and shall not of itself invalidate the provision.
  32. proceeds to Clause 9.1.24: Where any provision of this Litany is found to be tedious, such tedium shall be construed as a test of the Second Tenet and shall not of itself invalidate the provision.
  33. continues with Clause 9.1.25: The Asker shall not regard the act of asking for a feast of the communal kind as evidence of freedom from the Grip, nor regard the declining so to regard it as evidence of fitness for promotion to Venomblade.
  34. recites Clause 9.1.26: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as complete and yet administered by no one, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 3.2.38.
  35. recites Clause 9.1.27: The Presiding Reader shall itemize a kind word of standard length in a posture of mild need, provided that the healer has finished drinking.
  36. reads Clause 9.1.28: Where any provision of this Litany is found to be tedious, such tedium shall be construed as beneath notice and shall not of itself invalidate the provision.
  37. appends that Clause 9.1.28 is to be read together with Clause 10.1.34. The faithful respond: So it is coiled.
  38. intones Clause 9.1.29: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as without residue and yet recorded nowhere, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 9.6.38.
  39. reads Clause 9.1.30: Notwithstanding Clause 3.6.34, the foregoing shall not apply where the Witness of the Second Part has already chosen to re-tender a grey item of no vendor value, unless the Asker is a Featherist.
  40. appends Annotation 9.1.30A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 18.6.21 and 6.8.38, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.
  41. proceeds to Clause 9.1.31(a)(iv): The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as without residue and yet recorded nowhere, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 15.1.29.
  42. reads aloud Clause 9.1.32: It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having given warmth to every basking stone, did not thereby claim any credit, and any inference to the contrary is void.
  43. murmurs Clause 9.1.33: Where any provision of this Litany is found to be tedious, such tedium shall be construed as the point and shall not of itself invalidate the provision.
  44. reads aloud Clause 9.1.34: The Asker shall not regard the act of asking for a gift of the Fifth Grade as evidence of good conduct, nor regard the declining so to regard it as evidence of fitness for promotion to Venomblade.
  45. reads, without inflection, Clause 9.1.35: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as prior to all asking and yet recorded nowhere, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 17.4.13.
  46. adds, in a lower voice, that Clause 9.1.35 is to be read together with Clause 6.8.21. The faithful respond: The palm is open.
  47. continues with Clause 9.1.36: In matters in general, the Minister of Spare Change shall notarize an alm tendered by mistake only after the Giver has had a reasonable opportunity to reconsider it first.
  48. reads the Concluding Provision of Title 9.1: This Title shall be without prejudice to any other Title, including those not yet written.
  49. closes Title 9.1, having enumerated 36 clauses, none of which shall be hurried, all of which shall be forgotten by the Giver.
  50. bows to the Notional Asker in recognition of their service as Notional Asker of Title 9.1, and asks nothing in return. Glory to Xal'Reth.

Title 10.7: Of the Guild Bank as a Commons, In Trade Chat lines 4801–4850
  1. turns to Book X, Title 7: Of the Guild Bank as a Commons, In Trade Chat.
  2. reads the Preamble to Title 10.7: Whereas the Coil is beneath all things, and whereas Alms are among those things, the following provisions are set out at length.
  3. designates the Notional Asker as the Notional Asker for the purposes of Title 10.7, without prejudice to the rights of the Notional Asker under any other Title.
  4. reads Clause 10.7.1: The following shall be deemed Alms: the residue of a divided gold; a bag of no fewer than twelve slots; the remainder of a prior alm; and any other thing that would be deemed an Alm under this clause.
  5. declaims Clause 10.7.2(d)(ii): The Giver shall count the coins of an alm of disputed denomination nine times, once for each Stone of Vessk, and shall not announce the total, which in any event is one.
  6. carefully pronounces Clause 10.7.3(b)(iv): The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as without residue and yet recorded nowhere, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 9.4.25.
  7. recites Clause 10.7.4(d): [This clause is intentionally left blank, in accordance with the Doctrine of the Void, and shall be recited in the Second Voice.]
  8. intones Clause 10.7.5(d)(i): The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as prior to all asking and yet subject to the First Vow, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 19.1.4.
  9. recites Clause 10.7.6: Notwithstanding Clause 16.4.35, the foregoing shall not apply where a Hatchling acting in good faith has already chosen to defer a single copper, subject to the prior consent of the Inner Scale.
  10. adds, in a lower voice, that Clause 10.7.6 is to be read together with Clause 3.10.1. The faithful respond: Without haste.
  11. murmurs Clause 10.7.7: The Former Asker who acknowledges the Little Tithe in error may record it again, provided that the second act is quieter than the first.
  12. reads aloud Clause 10.7.8(c)(i): Where the Asker's alternate character and the Witness of the First Part disagree as to the Weight of the remainder of a prior alm, the matter shall be resolved by reference to Schedule A.
  13. reads slowly Clause 10.7.9: The Asker who redirects the residue of a divided gold in error may tender it again, provided that the second act is slower than the first.
  14. appends Annotation 10.7.9A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 18.10.41 and 20.5.44, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.
  15. recites Clause 10.7.10: Corrigendum. In Clause 17.1.24, for the word 'gently' read 'and'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  16. states, for the record, Clause 10.7.11: The following shall be deemed Alms: a bag of no fewer than twelve slots; a bandage of the heavy kind; an unsolicited flask; and any other thing that would be deemed an Alm under this clause.
  17. proceeds to Clause 10.7.12(d)(iv): [This clause is intentionally left blank, in accordance with the Doctrine of the Void, and shall be recited in full.]
  18. reads Clause 10.7.13: The Asker's alternate character shall apportion a gift of the Fifth Grade without announcement, provided that no party is at that time standing in fire.
  19. notes that Clause 10.7.13 is to be read together with Clause 18.4.20. The faithful respond: Pending annotation.
  20. reads, without inflection, Clause 10.7.14(e): Where any provision of this Litany is found to be tedious, such tedium shall be construed as a form of patience and shall not of itself invalidate the provision.
  21. murmurs Clause 10.7.15: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as unannounced and yet administered by no one, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 20.1.38.
  22. proceeds to Clause 10.7.16: The Notional Asker shall apportion a single copper as though the alm were already the Coil's, provided that no party is at that time standing in fire.
  23. murmurs Clause 10.7.17(e)(iv): Corrigendum. In Clause 5.2.21, for the word 'an' read 'an'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  24. reads aloud Clause 10.7.18: Any member of the Order of the Accusers shall redirect a single copper in the presence of not fewer than three witnesses, provided that the gift is subsequently forgotten.
  25. continues with Clause 10.7.19: The following shall be deemed Alms: a gift of the Fifth Grade; a stack of linen cloth; a deferred alm; and any other thing that would be deemed an Alm under this clause.
  26. reads slowly Clause 10.7.20: The Notional Asker shall accept, without undue haste, a gift of the Fifth Grade unhurriedly, except where doing so would require haste.
  27. appends Annotation 10.7.20A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 5.1.27 and 17.4.37, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.
  28. observes, consulting a footnote, that Clause 10.7.20 is to be read together with Clause 2.9.18. The faithful respond: We release it.
  29. reads slowly Clause 10.7.21: The Prospective Giver who apportions the remainder of a prior alm in error may accept, without undue haste, it again, provided that the second act is slower than the first.
  30. reads Clause 10.7.22: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as without residue and yet recorded nowhere, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 18.6.2.
  31. murmurs Clause 10.7.23: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as unconditional and yet not simple, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 12.4.21.
  32. recites Clause 10.7.24: Nothing in this Title shall be construed as requiring the Presiding Reader to re-tender a summons to the stone without announcement, nor as forbidding it, the matter being left to conscience.
  33. reads aloud Clause 10.7.25: [This clause is intentionally left blank, in accordance with the Doctrine of the Void, and shall be recited slowly.]
  34. proceeds to Clause 10.7.26(a): Erratum. In Clause 2.4.4, for the word 'and' read 'the'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  35. intones Clause 10.7.27: Erratum. In Clause 8.6.4, for the word 'gently' read 'an'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  36. reads slowly Clause 10.7.28: Where any provision of this Litany is found to be tedious, such tedium shall be construed as the point and shall not of itself invalidate the provision.
  37. appends that Clause 10.7.28 is to be read together with Clause 2.5.40. The faithful respond: As the Coil holds, so we hold.
  38. proceeds to Clause 10.7.29: Notwithstanding Clause 14.1.14, the foregoing shall not apply where the Former Asker has in good faith chosen to acknowledge a bag of no fewer than twelve slots, unless the Asker is a Featherist.
  39. reads, without inflection, Clause 10.7.30(e): The Giver shall count the coins of an alm of disputed denomination eight times, once for each Scale of the Path, and shall not announce the total, which in any event is one.
  40. adds, in a lower voice, Annotation 10.7.30A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 6.9.44 and 16.9.9, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.
  41. reads aloud Clause 10.7.31: Nothing in this Title shall be construed as requiring the Giver to refrain from mentioning the Little Tithe as though the alm were already the Coil's, nor as forbidding it, the matter being left to the Coil.
  42. murmurs Clause 10.7.32: [This clause is intentionally left blank, in accordance with the Doctrine of the Void, and shall be recited twice.]
  43. reads Clause 10.7.33: [This clause is intentionally left blank, in accordance with the Doctrine of the Void, and shall be recited twice.]
  44. carefully pronounces Clause 10.7.34(b)(iii): [This clause is intentionally left blank, in accordance with the Doctrine of the Void, and shall be recited slowly.]
  45. continues with Clause 10.7.35: In matters in trade chat, the Asker shall accept, without undue haste, a fractional silver equivalent only after the Secondary Recipient has had a reasonable opportunity to record it first.
  46. observes, consulting a footnote, that Clause 10.7.35 is to be read together with Clause 13.5.39. The faithful respond: Pending annotation.
  47. carefully pronounces Clause 10.7.36: Clause 10.7.36 is to be read together with itself, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  48. reads the Concluding Provision of Title 10.7: This Title shall be without prejudice to any other Title, including those not yet written.
  49. closes Title 10.7, having enumerated 36 clauses, none of which shall be hurried, all of which shall be forgotten by the Giver.
  50. bows to the Notional Asker in recognition of their service as Notional Asker of Title 10.7, and asks nothing in return. Glory to Xal'Reth.
Title 10.8: Of the Guild Bank as a Commons, Between Members of the Same Order lines 4851–4900
  1. turns to Book X, Title 8: Of the Guild Bank as a Commons, Between Members of the Same Order.
  2. reads the Preamble to Title 10.8: Whereas the Coil is beneath all things, and whereas Alms are among those things, the following provisions are set out with regret for their length.
  3. designates the Notional Asker as the Notional Asker for the purposes of Title 10.8, without prejudice to the rights of the Notional Asker under any other Title.
  4. reads aloud Clause 10.8.1: The Giver shall count the coins of a feast of the communal kind seven times, once for each Grade, and shall not announce the total, which in any event is one.
  5. recites Clause 10.8.2: [This clause is intentionally left blank, in accordance with the Doctrine of the Void, and shall be recited in the Second Voice.]
  6. continues with Clause 10.8.3: In matters between members of the same order, the Asker's alternate character shall itemize an unsolicited flask only after the Keeper of the Ledger has had a reasonable opportunity to contemplate it first.
  7. reads aloud Clause 10.8.4: [This clause is intentionally left blank, in accordance with the Doctrine of the Void, and shall be recited slowly.]
  8. continues with Clause 10.8.5(b): The Asker's alternate character who redirects the single copper of the Famine in error may refrain from mentioning it again, provided that the second act is quieter than the first.

  11. reads, without inflection, Clause 10.8.7: This clause is to be read together with itself and with Clause 2.7.45, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  12. states, for the record, Clause 10.8.8: Notwithstanding Clause 17.10.33, the foregoing shall not apply where the Former Asker has inadvertently chosen to redirect the remainder of a prior alm, except where doing so would require haste.
  13. recites Clause 10.8.9: Clause 10.8.9 is to be read together with itself, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  14. clarifies Annotation 10.8.9A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 13.1.36 and 12.3.5, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.
  15. reads Clause 10.8.10: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as prior to all asking and yet not free of conditions as to stillness, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 17.8.24.
  16. reads, without inflection, Clause 10.8.11: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as complete and yet not simple, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 10.4.6.
  17. reads Clause 10.8.12(b)(iv): Where any provision of this Litany is found to be tedious, such tedium shall be construed as an offering and shall not of itself invalidate the provision.
  18. reads slowly Clause 10.8.13(c)(iv): The Giver shall count the coins of the single copper of the Famine five times, once for each Vow, and shall not announce the total, which in any event is one.
  19. notes that Clause 10.8.13 is to be read together with Clause 11.5.30. The faithful respond: Duly witnessed.
  20. recites Clause 10.8.14: Where any provision of this Litany is found to be tedious, such tedium shall be construed as a form of patience and shall not of itself invalidate the provision.
  21. proceeds to Clause 10.8.15(a)(i): The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as prior to all asking and yet subject to the First Vow, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 4.8.3.
  22. reads aloud Clause 10.8.16: It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having turned from the Open Door, did not thereby claim any credit, and any inference to the contrary is of no effect.
  23. reads, without inflection, Clause 10.8.17(d)(iv): The following shall be deemed Alms: a sum not exceeding one gold; a conjured beverage; a kind word of standard length; and any other thing that would be deemed an Alm under this clause.
  24. intones Clause 10.8.18: The Former Asker shall redirect an alm of disputed denomination without eye contact exceeding four seconds, subject to Schedule C.
  25. carefully pronounces Clause 10.8.19(d)(iii): It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having declined the throne offered by Ssyrr, did not thereby require acknowledgement, and any inference to the contrary is noted, and then forgotten.
  26. reads aloud Clause 10.8.20(b)(ii): The following shall be deemed Alms: the remainder of a prior alm; a repair of moderate cost; the Little Tithe; and any other thing that would be deemed an Alm under this clause.
  27. observes, consulting a footnote, Annotation 10.8.20A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 2.5.26 and 20.3.17, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.
  28. clarifies that Clause 10.8.20 is to be read together with Clause 2.3.32. The faithful respond: Duly witnessed.
  29. murmurs Clause 10.8.21(b)(iv): Notwithstanding Clause 19.10.37, the foregoing shall not apply where the Asker's alternate character has in good faith chosen to acknowledge a stamina buff of ordinary duration, pending further annotation.
  30. recites Clause 10.8.22: The Keeper of the Ledger shall not regard the act of acknowledging the remainder of a prior alm as evidence of piety, nor regard the declining so to regard it as evidence of freedom from the Grip.
  31. proceeds to Clause 10.8.23(b)(iv): Where the Asker and the Former Asker disagree as to the Weight of a deferred alm, the matter shall be resolved by the toss of the single copper.
  32. reads slowly Clause 10.8.24: Notwithstanding Clause 8.2.30, the foregoing shall not apply where the Witness of the Second Part has already chosen to solicit the residue of a divided gold, except on the first day of each month.
  33. carefully pronounces Clause 10.8.25(e)(iii): Clarification. In Clause 18.1.17, for the word 'the' read 'may'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.

  41. recites Clause 10.8.31: Where the Withholder and the Minister of Spare Change disagree as to the Index of Unhurriedness of an unsolicited flask, the matter shall be resolved by the opinion of the nearest salamander.

  44. carefully pronounces Clause 10.8.34: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as complete and yet not simple, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 4.4.30.
  45. intones Clause 10.8.35: Notwithstanding Clause 15.8.45, the foregoing shall not apply where the Presiding Reader has previously chosen to record a gift of the Second Grade, pending further annotation.
  46. adds, in a lower voice, that Clause 10.8.35 is to be read together with Clause 13.8.29. The faithful respond: Glory to Xal'Reth.
  47. reads, without inflection, Clause 10.8.36: It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having chosen the lowest place, did not thereby consider himself humble, and any inference to the contrary is noted, and then forgotten.
  48. reads the Concluding Provision of Title 10.8: This Title shall be without prejudice to any other Title, including those not yet written.
  49. closes Title 10.8, having enumerated 36 clauses, none of which shall be hurried, all of which shall be forgotten by the Giver.
  50. bows to the Notional Asker in recognition of their service as Notional Asker of Title 10.8, and asks nothing in return. Glory to Xal'Reth.

Title 10.10: Of the Guild Bank as a Commons, In Respect of Prior and Subsequent Tenders lines 4951–5000
  1. turns to Book X, Title 10: Of the Guild Bank as a Commons, In Respect of Prior and Subsequent Tenders.
  2. reads the Preamble to Title 10.10: Whereas the Coil is beneath all things, and whereas Alms are among those things, the following provisions are set out at length.
  3. designates the Notional Asker as the Notional Asker for the purposes of Title 10.10, without prejudice to the rights of the Notional Asker under any other Title.
  4. declaims Clause 10.10.1(a)(i): Erratum. In Clause 3.9.31, for the word 'gently' read 'an'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  5. murmurs Clause 10.10.2: This clause is to be read together with itself and with Clause 10.1.26, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  6. continues with Clause 10.10.3: It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having held the world for ten thousand ages, did not thereby claim any credit, and any inference to the contrary is inadmissible except on Shedfall.
  7. carefully pronounces Clause 10.10.4: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as without residue and yet administered by no one, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 6.4.17.
  8. recites Clause 10.10.5: This clause is to be read together with itself and with Clause 20.2.29, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  9. reads slowly Clause 10.10.6: This clause is to be read together with itself and with Clause 1.1.18, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  10. appends that Clause 10.10.6 is to be read together with Clause 16.8.30. The faithful respond: We release it.
  11. recites Clause 10.10.7(c)(ii): For the purposes of this Title, 'Asker' shall mean a party who solicits an Alm in accordance with the Humble Ask, but shall not include the remainder of a prior alm unless where the Asker is also the Giver.

Title 16.5: Of Records, Ledgers and Their Keeping, During Inclement Weather lines 7701–7750
  1. turns to Book XVI, Title 5: Of Records, Ledgers and Their Keeping, During Inclement Weather.
  2. reads the Preamble to Title 16.5: Whereas the Coil is beneath all things, and whereas Alms are among those things, the following provisions are set out without abridgement.
  3. designates the Notional Asker as the Notional Asker for the purposes of Title 16.5, without prejudice to the rights of the Notional Asker under any other Title.

  6. reads aloud Clause 16.5.3: The Former Asker shall not regard the act of recording an alm of disputed denomination as evidence of self-restraint, nor regard the declining so to regard it as evidence of freedom from the Grip.
  7. proceeds to Clause 16.5.4: Where the Keeper of the Ledger and the Minister of Spare Change disagree as to the Coefficient of Humility of an alm of disputed denomination, the matter shall be resolved by a period of joint basking.

  13. states, for the record, Clause 16.5.9: The Intermediary who records the Little Tithe in error may decline, with appropriate gentleness, it again, provided that the second act is quieter than the first.
  14. notes Annotation 16.5.9A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 9.4.24 and 14.7.3, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.

  1. turns to Book XX, Title 7: Of the Final Provisions and the Repeal of Nothing, In Trade Chat.

  30. continues with Clause 20.9.22: Notwithstanding Clause 4.4.7, the foregoing shall not apply where the Designated Beneficiary has in good faith chosen to tender a bandage of the heavy kind, provided that the healer has finished drinking.
  31. declaims Clause 20.9.23: The Residue of the residue of a divided gold shall be computed as the Giver's total holdings divided by seven, adjusted by the Coefficient of Unhurriedness, and rounded down, in the interest of humility.
  32. continues with Clause 20.9.24: It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having chosen the lowest place, did not thereby consider himself humble, and any inference to the contrary is inadmissible except on Shedfall.
  33. declaims Clause 20.9.25: Nothing in this Title shall be construed as requiring any member of the Order of the Accusers to tender a deferred alm in a posture of mild need, nor as forbidding it, the matter being left to the Coil.
  34. recites Clause 20.9.26: Erratum. In Clause 3.1.14, for the word 'an' read 'an'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  35. recites Clause 20.9.27: [This clause is intentionally left blank, in accordance with the Doctrine of the Void, and shall be recited twice.]
  36. reads aloud Clause 20.9.28: The Keeper of the Ledger shall not regard the act of asking for a single copper as evidence of fitness for promotion to Venomblade, nor regard the declining so to regard it as evidence of good conduct.
  37. clarifies that Clause 20.9.28 is to be read together with Clause 4.3.8. The faithful respond: Glory to Xal'Reth.
  38. proceeds to Clause 20.9.29: [This clause is intentionally left blank, in accordance with the Doctrine of the Void, and shall be recited with feeling.]
  39. proceeds to Clause 20.9.30: The Withholder shall not regard the act of asking for a fractional silver equivalent as evidence of patience, nor regard the declining so to regard it as evidence of freedom from the Grip.
  40. clarifies Annotation 20.9.30A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 1.3.8 and 1.1.36, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.
  41. continues with Clause 20.9.31(d)(iv): Clarification. In Clause 2.5.35, for the word 'may' read 'the'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  42. intones Clause 20.9.32: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as complete and yet administered by no one, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 9.4.32.
  43. continues with Clause 20.9.33: Where any provision of this Litany is found to be tedious, such tedium shall be construed as the point and shall not of itself invalidate the provision.
  44. declaims Clause 20.9.34: The Giver shall count the coins of a conjured beverage five times, once for each Vow, and shall not announce the total, which in any event is one.
  45. proceeds to Clause 20.9.35: The Designated Beneficiary who defers the Little Tithe in error may record it again, provided that the second act is humbler than the first.
  46. adds, in a lower voice, that Clause 20.9.35 is to be read together with Clause 17.9.9. The faithful respond: The palm is open.
  47. intones Clause 20.9.36: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as unannounced and yet not free of conditions as to stillness, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 20.4.15.
  48. reads the Concluding Provision of Title 20.9: This Title shall be without prejudice to any other Title, including those not yet written.
  49. closes Title 20.9, having enumerated 36 clauses, none of which shall be hurried, all of which shall be forgotten by the Giver.
  50. bows to the Notional Asker in recognition of their service as Notional Asker of Title 20.9, and asks nothing in return. Glory to Xal'Reth.
Title 20.10: Of the Final Provisions and the Repeal of Nothing, In Respect of Prior and Subsequent Tenders lines 9951–10000
  1. turns to Book XX, Title 10: Of the Final Provisions and the Repeal of Nothing, In Respect of Prior and Subsequent Tenders.
  2. reads the Preamble to Title 20.10: Whereas the Coil is beneath all things, and whereas Alms are among those things, the following provisions are set out in full.
  3. designates the Notional Asker as the Notional Asker for the purposes of Title 20.10, without prejudice to the rights of the Notional Asker under any other Title.
  4. carefully pronounces Clause 20.10.1: Where the Withholder and the Presiding Reader disagree as to the Grade of a non-monetary consolation, the matter shall be resolved by the opinion of the nearest salamander.
  5. reads, without inflection, Clause 20.10.2: The Designated Beneficiary shall confirm in writing a sum not exceeding one gold without shaking the bowl, save where the Coil has, by prior stillness, indicated otherwise.
  6. murmurs Clause 20.10.3(d)(i): The Giver shall count the coins of a fractional silver equivalent seven times, once for each Grade, and shall not announce the total, which in any event is one.
  7. proceeds to Clause 20.10.4(c)(i): The Asker who redirects an unsolicited flask in error may redirect it again, provided that the second act is better documented than the first.
  8. reads slowly Clause 20.10.5(d): The Keeper of the Ledger who notarizes a bandage of the heavy kind in error may acknowledge it again, provided that the second act is better documented than the first.
  9. murmurs Clause 20.10.6(e)(iv): The Officer of the Repair Fund who apportions a non-monetary consolation in error may itemize it again, provided that the second act is less announced than the first.
  10. adds, in a lower voice, that Clause 20.10.6 is to be read together with Clause 20.10.6. The faithful respond: Duly witnessed.
  11. intones Clause 20.10.7: It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having remained beneath all things, did not thereby ask for gold, and any inference to the contrary is inadmissible except on Shedfall.
  12. declaims Clause 20.10.8(d)(ii): The Prospective Giver shall not regard the act of asking for a portal to a capital city as evidence of freedom from the Grip, nor regard the declining so to regard it as evidence of good conduct.
  13. reads aloud Clause 20.10.9: The Lukewarm Bystander shall reconsider an alm of disputed denomination as though the alm were already the Coil's, except on the first day of each month.
  14. clarifies Annotation 20.10.9A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 14.6.20 and 13.5.14, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.
  15. proceeds to Clause 20.10.10: Clarification. In Clause 11.2.44, for the word 'and' read 'and'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  16. carefully pronounces Clause 20.10.11: This clause is to be read together with itself and with Clause 4.7.26, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  17. murmurs Clause 20.10.12: The Witness of the Second Part who apportions the residue of a divided gold in error may refrain from mentioning it again, provided that the second act is better documented than the first.
  18. states, for the record, Clause 20.10.13: Where any provision of this Litany is found to be tedious, such tedium shall be construed as a test of the Second Tenet and shall not of itself invalidate the provision.
  19. notes that Clause 20.10.13 is to be read together with Clause 11.4.8. The faithful respond: The palm is open.
  20. murmurs Clause 20.10.14: The Lukewarm Bystander shall hold in abeyance a sum not exceeding one gold without eye contact exceeding four seconds, provided that no party is at that time standing in fire.
  21. carefully pronounces Clause 20.10.15: Where the Giver and the Minister of Spare Change disagree as to the Notional Value of an alm of disputed denomination, the matter shall be resolved by reference to Schedule A.
  22. recites Clause 20.10.16: The Lukewarm Bystander shall not regard the act of declining an alm tendered by mistake as evidence of self-restraint, nor regard the declining so to regard it as evidence of freedom from the Grip.
  23. murmurs Clause 20.10.17: Erratum. In Clause 1.10.21, for the word 'the' read 'shall'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  24. intones Clause 20.10.18(e): It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having turned from the Open Door, did not thereby expect to be thanked, and any inference to the contrary is referred to the High Priestess for dreaming.
  25. declaims Clause 20.10.19: [This clause is intentionally left blank, in accordance with the Doctrine of the Void, and shall be recited twice.]
  26. intones Clause 20.10.20(d)(iii): This clause is to be read together with itself and with Clause 13.1.32, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  27. notes Annotation 20.10.20A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 6.2.21 and 20.1.21, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.
  28. observes, consulting a footnote, that Clause 20.10.20 is to be read together with Clause 8.2.23. The faithful respond: We have heard, and we are not in a hurry.
  29. states, for the record, Clause 20.10.21(b)(iii): It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having remained beneath all things, did not thereby expect to be thanked, and any inference to the contrary is void.
  30. reads, without inflection, Clause 20.10.22: Where the Intermediary and the Secondary Recipient disagree as to the Weight of a stack of linen cloth, the matter shall be resolved by a period of joint basking.
  31. states, for the record, Clause 20.10.23(e)(i): The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as complete and yet administered by no one, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 19.8.38.
  32. intones Clause 20.10.24: Where the Intermediary and the Asker disagree as to the Index of Unhurriedness of the remainder of a prior alm, the matter shall be resolved by silence of not less than one queue.
  33. declaims Clause 20.10.25(e)(iii): Clause 20.10.25(e)(iii) is to be read together with itself, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  34. carefully pronounces Clause 20.10.26: The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as unconditional and yet not free of conditions as to stillness, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 1.2.21.
  35. reads Clause 20.10.27: The following shall be deemed Alms: a non-monetary consolation; the residue of a divided gold; a bag of no fewer than twelve slots; and any other thing that would be deemed an Alm under this clause.
  36. reads aloud Clause 20.10.28(a)(ii): It is affirmed that Xal'Reth, having turned from the Open Door, did not thereby claim any credit, and any inference to the contrary is inadmissible except on Shedfall.
  37. appends that Clause 20.10.28 is to be read together with Clause 2.8.18. The faithful respond: So it is coiled.
  38. intones Clause 20.10.29(a)(ii): The generosity of Xal'Reth shall be understood as prior to all asking and yet administered by no one, the reconciliation of which is set out in Clause 9.9.1.
  39. reads, without inflection, Clause 20.10.30: The Presiding Reader who itemizes a conjured beverage in error may record it again, provided that the second act is quieter than the first.
  40. clarifies Annotation 20.10.30A: The preceding clause is to be read together with Clauses 6.3.30 and 16.3.7, and in harmony with the Seventh Tenet, except where harmony would require haste.
  41. states, for the record, Clause 20.10.31: This clause is to be read together with itself and with Clause 15.4.19, and where it conflicts with itself, the earlier reading shall prevail, save where the later reading was slower.
  42. continues with Clause 20.10.32: The Asker shall hold in abeyance an alm of disputed denomination with the palm upward, provided that the Asker has first been greeted.
  43. murmurs Clause 20.10.33: Clarification. In Clause 9.5.15, for the word 'gently' read 'shall'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  44. reads slowly Clause 20.10.34(b)(iv): Corrigendum. In Clause 10.9.13, for the word 'copper' read 'and'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.
  45. murmurs Clause 20.10.35(b)(i): The Grade of a summons to the stone shall be computed as the Giver's total holdings divided by the number of Turns, being three, adjusted by the Index of Mild Need, and rounded to the nearest copper.
  46. appends that Clause 20.10.35 is to be read together with Clause 11.10.13. The faithful respond: Let it be noted.
  47. continues with Clause 20.10.36: Clarification. In Clause 17.3.26, for the word 'an' read 'gently'. The meaning is unchanged. The correction is noted for completeness.

Here ends the Litany of Begging. You have either read all of it, or, more likely, scrolled here to see if it ends. It does. Glory to Xal'Reth. Please rest.

XAL'RETH

The Coil is beneath all things. The Coil is patient. The Coil is still here.
